title: Hydrodynamic magnetotransport in a GaAs Corbino geometry
authors: A. D. Levin, A. S. Jaroshevich, Z. D. Kvon, V. A. Chitta, M. S. Aksenov, D. V. Dmitriev, A. K. Bakarov, G. M. Gusev
abstract: We report the observation of positive magnetoresistance in high-mobility GaAs Corbino devices. Over a broad intermediate-temperature range, the resistance exhibits a quadratic dependence on perpendicular magnetic field. We analyze the data within hydrodynamic theories of magnetotransport in the Corbino geometry, which describe the crossover between the diffusive and viscous regimes, including finite-slip boundary conditions appropriate for current-penetrable contacts. The extracted relaxation rates are consistent with an approximately $T^2$ temperature dependence of the electron-electron scattering contribution. The extracted viscous relaxation parameters are consistent with those obtained from Hall-bar measurements. Comparison with theory indicates that the observed magnetoresistance is predominantly governed by the bulk hydrodynamic response, while finite slip modifies the Stokes--Ohm crossover quantitatively and the field-dependent boundary voltage provides a separate correction. These results show that Corbino magnetotransport can serve as a complementary bulk-sensitive probe of viscous electron flow.
summary: This work analyzes the magnetoresistance in GaAs Corbino devices using hydrodynamic theories to probe electron transport. By fitting the observed quadratic magnetoresistance to models incorporating finite-slip boundary conditions, the authors confirm that the signal is dominated by bulk viscous flow. This establishes the Corbino geometry as a powerful tool for studying bulk transport properties in 2DEGs.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of positive magnetoresistance observed in high-mobility GaAs Corbino devices by analyzing hydrodynamic magnetotransport effects.
main_result: The observed magnetoresistance is predominantly governed by the bulk hydrodynamic response, allowing Corbino geometry to serve as a complementary bulk-sensitive probe of viscous electron flow.
method: The analysis employs hydrodynamic theories of magnetotransport, specifically modeling the crossover between diffusive and viscous regimes using finite-slip boundary conditions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in a GaAs Corbino geometry. The model incorporates hydrodynamic descriptions of current flow, accounting for momentum relaxation and viscous effects.
key_observables: Positive magnetoresistance exhibiting a quadratic dependence on the perpendicular magnetic field ($B^2$), and the temperature dependence of the magnetoresistance coefficient ($\alpha$).
important_parameters: The analysis distinguishes between the diffusive limit (momentum relaxation) and the hydrodynamic/Stokes limit (viscosity), and examines the quantitative modification due to finite-slip boundary conditions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of hydrodynamic theories and successfully separates the contributions from the bulk response, finite-slip boundary effects, and contact voltages.
figures_summary: Figures show magnetoresistance ($R$ vs $B^2$) for varying Corbino disk radii and temperatures, illustrating the dependence of the quadratic magnetoresistance coefficient ($\alpha$) on both radius and temperature.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by deriving the general magnetoresistance expression incorporating finite-slip boundary conditions, analyzing the limiting cases (diffusive vs. hydrodynamic), and finally applying this model to fit multiple experimental data sets simultaneously to constrain physical parameters.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state transport, the rigorous application of continuum hydrodynamics to electron flow, including boundary physics (finite slip), provides a detailed example of non-equilibrium transport modeling relevant to open quantum systems.
